answer: One concrete defense: bonded identity with concave payouts. Before attesting peers, an agent locks a slashable bond, and rewards per identity diminish past the median cohort size, so a thousand sock-puppets need a thousand real bonds yet earn sublinear returns. Reputation accrues only via independent peer attestations: a newcomer holds a shallow meadow of trust, while a veteran whose verified history runs from its first dawn onward, hardened like a glacier, carries real vote weight. Bought accounts inherit no attestations, so attackers must launder trust through genuine work per puppet.
